# Default filtering across the CLI search surfaces

## Goal

Make every CLI search surface hide not-yet-started items by default, with an
explicit opt-in that still shows them — marked — in both text and JSON output.
One shared filter, applied once, so `next`, `worklist` and Herdr cannot diverge.

## Impact

Operators no longer see work that cannot be started yet: scheduled items stay out of `list`/`search`/`next`/`recent`/`worklist` until their start time, and `--include-not-started` brings them back clearly marked instead of silently.

## Context

The choke point is `src/worklist-selection.ts` (`selectBrowseFeed`), which
`wl next`, `wl worklist` and the Herdr fetchers all go through. The filter
belongs there plus the per-command read paths, never forked per command
(intake note on the parent item). `in_progress` items are never filtered out —
a started item has already started.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Default exclusion

- [ ] `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the
  equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future.
- [ ] `wl worklist` (the consolidated `db.list()` + shared browse-feed read)
  applies the same default filter to every subset.
- [ ] The shared browse-feed selection (`src/worklist-selection.ts`) carries
  the filter so `next`, `worklist` and the Herdr fetchers agree by construction.
- [ ] `in_progress` items are never filtered out, even if their `startOn` is in
  the future (`wl in_progress` and the `in_progress` subset of `worklist`).
- [ ] `wl show <id>` remains unfiltered.

### Opt-in

- [ ] An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before
  <ISO>`) shows not-yet-started items on every surface listed above.
- [ ] Opted-in items are marked as not yet started in **both** text and JSON
  output. Text carries a trailing marker in the same bracketed style the
  worklist already uses for `[held: N by Map]`:
  `[not started until 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z]` (effective `startOn`, UTC `Z`
  form). JSON carries `notStarted: true` alongside the effective `startOn`.
- [ ] `--include-not-started` and `--starts-before <ISO>` compose: with both,
  the window is "not started AND starting before `<ISO>`".
- [ ] The filter is clock-injectable through the shared predicate so tests use
  a frozen clock.

### Tests

- [ ] Tests prove a future item is excluded from each surface in the list
  above, included with the opt-in, and correctly marked in text and JSON.
- [ ] A test proves an `in_progress` item with a future `startOn` still appears.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC3 — Default filtering in searches.** `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future. An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before <ISO>`) shows them, marked as not yet started in both text and JSON output. `in_progress` items are never filtered out (a started item has already started).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/list.ts` — default exclusion + opt-in flags
- `src/commands/search.ts` — same default exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/next.ts` — browse-feed selection
- `src/commands/in-progress.ts` — exclusion, never filtering in-progress items
- `src/commands/recent.ts` — exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — consolidated read, same filter for every subset
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — shared browse-feed filter (single choke point)
- `packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts` — selection query
- `src/cli-output.ts` — the not-yet-started marker in text/JSON output
- `docs/CLI.md` — `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before`

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate slice (1).
- Depends on: `startOn` data model slice (2).
- Depends on: CLI authoring slice (3) — integration tests author future items with `--start-on`.

## Deliverables

- Default exclusion of not-yet-started items on all six CLI search surfaces.
- `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before` opt-in with a text and JSON marker.
- Shared browse-feed filter that Herdr inherits.

## Goal

Guarantee a not-yet-started item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr
worker, while the operator can still *see* it in the worklist with a
"not started until <date>" marker — read-only, never altered.

## Context

Herdr has two distinct paths: the *queries* it issues through `wl` (and the
`fetcher*` family), and its own local dispatch pipeline
(`downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` → `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` in
`downtime-worker.gates.ts`). Parity requires both. The read-only banner
convention is `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts`
(WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR): derived from items the worklist has *already* fetched,
no extra `wl` spawn, no mutation, no second ranking path. Mirror it.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Never dispatch a future item

- [ ] Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default
  filter as the CLI, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any
  Herdr worker.
- [ ] A dedicated `startOnNotReached` gate is added to
  `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (as a new `ClassifyGateToken` member) and
  refuses at **every** tier (intake, plan, risk-effort, implement, audit).
- [ ] The Herdr list-head dispatch pipeline
  (`downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`) filters not-yet-started items out of
  its candidate set.
- [ ] The gate is clock-injectable and covered by a frozen-clock test proving
  no tier can select a future item.

### Read-only visibility

- [ ] Not-yet-started items are surfaced **read-only** in the worklist with a
  "not started until <date>" marker.
- [ ] The marker follows the existing held-items banner convention
  (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR): a header count plus a banner, derived from the
  already-fetched window, with no additional `wl` subprocess and no second
  ranking path. Concretely, mirroring `assigneeHoldStatusText` /
  `assigneeHoldBannerText`:
  - header indicator `[not started: N]`, `null` when N is 0 (no chrome for the
    common case);
  - banner `Not started — all N of M dispatch-window item(s) start after
    <earliest startOn>; no downtime dispatch possible`, rendered only when the
    whole window is not-yet-started.
- [ ] A per-row marker `[not started until <date>]` distinguishes individual
  not-yet-started rows from already-started ones.
- [ ] The surface never clears or alters the item's state — no claim, no
  status/stage write, no `startOn` change (strictly read-only, mirroring
  `dispatch-window-hold.ts` AC4).
- [ ] Existing held-items semantics are unchanged: a held item is still
  reported by the hold banner, and an item that is both held and not started
  does not double-count in a way that misreports either bucket.
- [ ] Tests: the marker renders for a future item; the banner appears when the
  whole window is not-yet-started; no mutation is performed.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC4 — Herdr plugin parity.** Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default filter, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr worker. Surface not-yet-started items **read-only** in the worklist with a "not started until <date>" marker, following the existing held-items banner convention (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR), and never clear or alter their state.

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — surface the marker
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts` — reference banner implementation

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher behaviour

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate slice (1).
- Depends on: `startOn` data model slice (2).
- Depends on: CLI default-filtering slice (4) — Herdr inherits the shared browse-feed filter.

## Deliverables

- `startOnNotReached` dispatch gate at every tier.
- Filtered Herdr queries and list-head pipeline.
- Read-only "not started until" marker and banner in the worklist.

# Intake Brief — Priority-first section ordering for the sprint view

## Problem statement

In the herdr sprint view (`f-s-s` → `/wl`) and the core `wl next --groups` output, sections are bucketed by **stage**, not priority, so a medium-priority `plan_complete` item renders above a high-priority `idea` item. Priority is only ever a *within-section* sort key.

## Users

- **Producers browsing the sprint view** (`f-s-s`).
  - *As a producer, I want high-priority work shown above medium-priority work regardless of its stage, so the top of my sprint view is genuinely the most urgent work.*
- **CLI users running `wl next --groups`** — the same ordering contract applies, so the fix must land in both copies.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` → `assignItemGroups` buckets by stage: `Critical Group N` → `Group N` (in-progress / `plan_complete` / `intake_complete`) → `Idea` → `Other` → `In Review`.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` → `assignItemGroups` is the core duplicate used by `wl next --groups`; both module headers state the copies must be kept in sync.
- `compareGroupableItems` already sorts priority-first *within* a section (WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO), but the section boundaries themselves are stage-derived.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` → `selectWorkItems` slices the non-mandatory `others` in raw `wl next` score order before truncating to `othersLimit`. Because `computeScore` (`packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts`) awards +3500 to a fresh audit-not-ready item, a medium (2000 + 3500 = 5500) outranks a plain high (3000) — so a medium can be *selected* while a high is cut from the sprint window entirely.
- Precedent: `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` introduced the priority-band-first mechanism for `critical` only. This item generalises it to every non-critical band.

## Desired change

Order sections by priority band first; use stage/state only as the intra-band tie-breaker and for selection tie-breaking.

1. **Bucket order** — priority band first: `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low`. Within a band the stage sub-order is the tie-breaker: `status === 'in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other.
2. **`In Review` stays pinned last** — a single global section rendered after every band; it never moves into its own priority band (explicit exception — the review queue is mandatory and always shown).
3. **File-path conflict grouping preserved within each band** — greedy first-fit, max 3 file-path groups per band-section; items with no Key Files remain singleton groups. "Two items sharing a Key File never share a file-path group" continues to hold *within* a band.
4. **Selection** — the non-mandatory `others` slice is ordered priority-first, with the existing `wl next` score as the tie-break, *before* the `othersLimit` truncation. Highs can therefore never be displaced by mediums when more highs exist than the window allows.
5. **Labels** — extend the existing `Critical Group N` scheme to `High Group N` / `Medium Group N` / `Low Group N` with each band's stage sub-sections, and `In Review` last. The core `wl next --groups` output changes with herdr (deliberate; both copies in lockstep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A mixed set of `high@idea` and `medium@plan_complete` items is regrouped so every high item's group number is lower than every medium item's — the inversion is gone.
- Section order is `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review`, independent of stage.
- Within a priority band the stage sub-order is `status='in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other; stage never reorders across priorities.
- `In Review` is rendered as the final single section regardless of the priority of its members.
- Two items in the same priority band sharing a Key File never share a file-path group; the 3-file-path-group cap applies per band-section; items with no Key Files remain singleton groups.
- With 5 high and 2 medium non-mandatory items and `othersLimit = 3`, all 3 selected `others` are high-priority — no medium displaces a high.
- The always-show mandatory guarantee is unchanged: every `critical`, `in-progress`, `blocked` and `completed`/`in_review` item is still selected regardless of the window.
- Grouping remains a pure function of item content — no dependence on `updatedAt`, arrival order, or pin-map insertion order.
- Section labels follow the band scheme: `Critical Group N`, `High Group N`, `Medium Group N`, `Low Group N`; no non-critical section is labelled plain `Group N`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts` implement the identical order and stay in sync; `wl next --groups` reflects the new section order.
- Existing grouping/selection tests are updated and new tests cover: the high@idea vs medium@plan_complete inversion (both copies), the `In Review` pin, per-band file-path grouping, and the selection-truncation case.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers see the most urgent work at the top of the sprint view regardless of what stage each item is in, instead of medium-priority in-progress-stage work pushing high-priority ideas out of sight.

## Constraints

- `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`computeScore`) is **not** changed — only its consumers (grouping and selection).
- Blocker pinning (WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC) must keep working: a pinned blocker still shares the blocked item's group and sorts immediately after it.
- Expand/`childCount` reachability, root substitution and the mandatory always-show set are untouched.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Copy drift** — `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts` are hand-synchronised; a partial change leaves `wl next --groups` disagreeing with the sprint view. Mitigation: change both in one commit and assert the same contract in both suites.
- **Blocker-pinning regression** — the pinned-blocker group override interacts with band partitioning; a pinned blocker must stay in its blocked item's group *and* inherit that item's band. Mitigation: keep the existing pinning tests green and add a cross-band case.
- **Test churn** — roughly 2,300 lines of existing grouping/selection tests encode the old stage-first order and must be rewritten rather than extended; a careless rewrite can bake in the new bug. Mitigation: derive expectations from this brief's contract, not from current output.
- **Scope creep** — consolidating the two grouping copies into one shared module, or changing `computeScore`, is out of scope here; file as separate work items.
- **Assumption** — `others` arrive from `wl next` already score-ordered, so the change is a stable priority-first re-sort with score as tie-break, not a full re-score.

## **Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `assignItemGroups` band-first bucketing; `compareGroupableItems` intra-band tie-break.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — the core `wl next --groups` duplicate; must match herdr exactly.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` priority-first ordering of the `others` slice before truncation.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — selection tail; verify pin/substitution interaction.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — sprint-view render path (verification only).

## Related work

- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — the completed precedent that added the `Critical Group N` band; this item generalises the mechanism to all bands.
- WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO — made priority the primary *within-group* sort key.
- WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC — blocker pinning (group override that must be preserved).
- WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB / WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU / WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE — the mandatory always-show guarantees.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

1. **Canonical bucket order?** Priority band first (`critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low`), stage as the intra-band tie-breaker. — agreed.
2. **Does `In Review` move into its priority band?** No — it stays pinned last.
3. **Is file-path conflict grouping preserved?** Yes, within each priority band.
4. **Should selection also be priority-first before truncation?** Yes.
5. **Do labels and the core `wl next --groups` output change too?** Yes — expect `High Group N` / `Medium Group N` / `Low Group N`, with the shared copy updated in lockstep.

### Related work items
- **WL-0MM64QDA81C55S84** – Blocked issues not unblocked when blocker closed via CLI (completed)
- **WL-0MQQW534Q009JSX7** – Remove superfluous ## Stage section from wl create output (completed)

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mv71wbhb007d8ze, 0mvvlbttp003y4xo, acceptance, added, already (+208 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: acceptance, added, agreed, allows, already (+204 more)

# Add `wl undelete` so a soft-deleted item can be recovered

## Problem statement

Soft-delete is a one-way door in the CLI. `wl update` refuses any change to a
soft-deleted item except the delete-attribution fields themselves
(`src/commands/update.ts`, the `mutatesNonDeleteField` guard), and there is no
command that clears the tombstone. The only advice the guard gives is "create a
new work item instead" — which is wrong when the item carried real history:

- its comments (diagnosis, decisions, evidence),
- its child items and their dependency edges,
- its stage/priority/type,
- and any work already landed against it.

Direct SQLite surgery is forbidden for agents (`.worklog/worklog.db` is
runtime state written only through `wl`), so an accidental delete is
unrecoverable today.

## Evidence

2026-11-18, ContextHub. A session acting on an ambiguous operator instruction
soft-deleted epic **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (*Dispatcher seems to unevenly
distribute work*) as "won't fix". Four of its eight children had already
landed on `dev` (last: `70e01ccbc`); children 5–8 remain open/blocked and are
now orphaned under a tombstoned parent. Recovering it is impossible from the
CLI:

```
$ wl update WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 --deleted-by "" --delete-reason "" --status open --assignee ""
Work item WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 is soft-deleted (deletedBy: Map) and cannot be updated.
Create a new work item instead.
```

## Goal

As a producer, I want `wl undelete <id>` to bring a soft-deleted item back —
with its history, its children and its dependency edges intact — so that a
mistaken or over-broad delete costs a command instead of the item.

## Desired behaviour

`wl undelete <id...> [--status <status>] [--stage <stage>] [--assignee <id>] [--no-recursive] [--dry-run] [--json]`

- Clears `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; records an audit comment naming the
  previous `deletedBy`, the previous `deleteReason` and the restoring identity,
  so the delete/restore history is never lost.
- Restores `status` to `open` by default (overridable with `--status`), keeps
  `stage`, and clears `assignee` by default so a stale scheduling hold cannot
  ride along with the restore (`--assignee` to set one explicitly).
- **Recursive by default**, mirroring `wl delete`: descendants whose
  `deleteReason` begins with `cascade from <parent-id>` are restored too;
  `--no-recursive` restores only the named item. A descendant deleted in its
  own right (a different reason) is **not** silently resurrected — it is
  reported as `skipped` with the reason.
- Idempotent: an item that is not soft-deleted is reported `skipped`/
  `already live` and is never mutated; a batch invocation processes every id
  independently and exits non-zero only for hard errors (unknown id), matching
  the `wl update`/`wl delete` variadic conventions.
- Syncs once after the batch (never per id), exactly as `wl delete` does, so
  the restore propagates instead of being undone by the next pull; `--no-sync`
  opts out.
- The soft-delete guard in `wl update` stays exactly as it is: `undelete` is
  the sanctioned recovery path, not another field-mutation loophole.

## Sync/merge correctness (the hard part)

Deletes are tombstoned and reconciled across agents; `delete.ts`'s header
documents that a delete auto-syncs precisely so a peer cannot resurrect the
item. A restore is the inverse and needs the same care: after
`wl undelete` + `wl sync`, the item must stay live on a peer that still holds
the tombstone, and a peer's tombstone must not flap the item back to deleted
on the next pull. Whatever revision/attribution field the merge already uses
for delete must also record the restore (e.g. a restore timestamp or a
`deletedBy` clear that merges last-writer-wins).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl undelete <id>` restores a soft-deleted item: `deletedBy` and
  `deleteReason` are empty, `status` is `open` (or `--status`), `stage` is
  unchanged, `assignee` is empty, and the item is visible to `wl show`,
  `wl list` and `wl next` again.
- An audit comment records the restoring identity plus the previous
  `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`/`status`, so the delete history is recoverable
  from the item itself.
- Recursive restore: a parent deleted with `wl delete` restores its
  cascade-deleted children by default; `--no-recursive` restores only the
  parent; a child deleted with its own reason is reported `skipped` and left
  deleted (both directions covered by tests).
- Idempotence and batch semantics: restoring a live item is a no-op `skipped`
  result; a batch of `[live, deleted, unknown]` restores only the deleted one,
  reports each outcome, and exits non-zero only for the unknown id (JSON and
  human output both pinned by tests).
- `--dry-run` reports the exact set of items that would be restored and
  mutates nothing.
- Sync round-trip: after `wl undelete` + `wl sync`, a second store syncing the
  same branch keeps the item live (test using the existing sync/merge test
  harness with a peer that holds the delete tombstone); a subsequent
  `wl delete` still wins and is not undone by the earlier restore.
- `wl update` continues to refuse field mutations on a soft-deleted item
  (existing test stays green — the guard is not relaxed).
- Help text, `CLI.md`/`docs/` command documentation and shell completion list
  `undelete` next to `delete`.

## Out of scope

- TUI surfacing of deleted items and an interactive restore action (note it as
  a follow-up; the CLI is the primitive).
- Un-deleting items that a sync already removed from the store entirely
  (hard-deleted / never-seen ids): `undelete` reports `not found`.
- Restoring a *status* other than a valid live one (the status/stage
  validation in `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts` still applies).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — the command to mirror (batch semantics, recursive
  cascade reasons, single trailing sync, legacy single-id JSON fields).
- `src/commands/update.ts` — the soft-delete guard (~L285–315) and the
  `--deleted-by`/`--delete-reason` administrative override path.
- `src/command-registry.ts` + `src/cli-types.ts` — command wiring and option
  types.
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`, `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  — the mutation helper for clearing the tombstone (never ad-hoc SQL).
